chunks: And Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding one who catches a bird in the Haram, he said:
"If it is sound of wing, then let it go. And if it is not sound of wing, he should tend to it, feed it, and give it water; then when its two wings become restored, he should release it."

key_terms.أَطْعَمَهُ: he should feed it and care for its nourishment
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary in which hunting and harming game are prohibited
key_terms.خَلَّى عَنْهُ: he should let it go and release it
key_terms.طَيْرًا: a bird or game bird caught within the sanctuary
key_terms.غَيْرَ مُسْتَوِي الْجَنَاحِ: having damaged or not yet properly restored wings
key_terms.مُسْتَوِيَ الْجَنَاحِ: having sound, intact, or properly restored wings

ai.seo_question: What should be done if someone catches an injured or uninjured bird in the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a bird caught within the Haram. If the bird is unharmed, it must be released immediately; if it is injured, it must be cared for until it recovers and then released, reflecting the sanctity of the Haram and the protection due to its creatures.
